research_rationale:
basis_pattern: original_plus_bounded_search. EO 13251 (signed 2001-12-28; 67 FR 1599; official Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13251.txt, read in full) prescribes the order in which officers of the Department of State act as Secretary of State when the Secretary cannot serve, states exceptions, and revokes Executive Order 12343. Identity: the Title 3 heading of Executive Order 13251 of December 28, 2001, on an order of succession within the Department of State at 67 FR 1599, the title and the date agree with the register row. The dossier inventory has thirty-eight clauses (the lead-in, sections 1 to 4 and their lettered and numbered paragraphs); I confirmed it without correction. Own terms: no clause of sections 1 to 3 has an end date or ending condition; section 4 is a self-executing revocation of EO 12343 performed on issuance and recorded as terminated on 2001-12-28; section 3(b) was replaced by EO 13261. Later instruments: a search of every held order text for the number 13251 finds EO 13261 (replacing section 3(b), attached as a later event), the order's own Federal Register copy and a 2010 Federal Register document whose authority line reads Executive Order 13251 dated November 24, 2009, which is a miscitation of another order and not an instrument affecting this one; no held text revokes or supersedes it. The three selected machine searches (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) were read with their coverage notes, carry no coverage warning, and record 1, 1 and 1 hits for the order number respectively. Limit stated plainly: the continuing predicate rests on the held original text, the held amendment and the bounded searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09); the text of 22 U.S.C. 2651a and of the Vacancies Act as now codified is not held, and the held evidence does not show whether any listed office was renamed or abolished (section 3(d) deems a successor office to be the position).
